info.title: PowerApps API
info.description:
The PowerApps API serves the maker and admin surface for canvas apps and connectors — listing apps in an environment, reading connector metadata and definitions, and inspecting connections, environments and gateways.

Connector paths require an environment `$filter`; app paths accept a narrower, non-OData filter grammar. The service accepts a wide range of `api-version` values that largely behave as routing labels rather than distinct contracts.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/powerapps) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

One app or connector route is commonly addressable three ways, and clients build the path rather than hard-coding it: `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps` + optionally `/scopes/admin` + optionally `/environments/{environmentId}` + the resource path. The admin scope reads across a tenant without being shared on the resource; the environment segment narrows the same call. Not every combination exists for every resource, so only the forms actually witnessed are written out under `paths`.

`info.x-ppapi-migration` carries the admin centre's own table of legacy routes on this host and their Power Platform API replacements — including many routes whose HTTP method no client here reveals.
info.x-probe-tenant: Probed 2026-08-27 against a production tenant with 14 environments, 21 connections, 1710 catalogue connectors and 0 canvas apps. All probes were read-only GETs; nothing was created or modified.

x-ppapi-migration.description: The admin centre ships a route table that rewrites legacy `api.powerapps.com` paths onto the Power Platform API, and turns the rewrite on with a `deprecateLegacyPARP` flag. It is the service's own statement of which of these routes are being retired and what replaces each one, so it is recorded verbatim rather than turned into operations: the table names paths and targets, and for all but three entries it does not name a method, which is why most of these paths do not appear under `paths`.
x-ppapi-migration.note: `namespace` says which of those two hosts serves the replacement; see spec:ppapi for the host construction. A path listed here still answers on api.powerapps.com today — the flag controls which one the admin centre calls, not which one exists.

tags.name: Canvas App
tags.description: Canvas apps: the drag-and-drop apps makers build in Power Apps Studio. Model-driven apps are Dataverse solution components and are not served here.

tags.name: Connection
tags.description: Connection instances: a user's stored, authenticated binding to one connector in one environment. Where the connector catalogue says what could be used, these say what is.

tags.name: Connector
tags.description: The connector catalogue — called 'apis' on the wire. What a maker in a given environment could connect to, with the licensing tier and capability metadata that DLP policies and licence checks are built on.

tags.name: Environment
tags.description: Environments in the PowerApps API's own projection, which differs from BAPI's: it carries the cluster, the per-service runtime endpoints and the caller's capability map, and omits BAPI's provisioning fields.

tags.name: Gateway
tags.description: On-premises data gateways, which let cloud connectors reach data behind a corporate firewall.

tags.name: Notification
tags.description: In-product notifications the Power Apps surfaces raise for a user — the message centre behind the bell icon, not Entra or Graph notifications.

get.description:
Lists the connector catalogue as it applies to one environment: the ~1700 first-party, certified-publisher and independent-publisher connectors a maker in that environment could use. The environment `$filter` is mandatory.

The governance fields BAPI exposes as `unblockableConnectorsMetadata` and `virtualConnectorsMetadata` are *not* returned here; a caller that needs them has to read them from BAPI and merge.

The three boolean flags are additive filters over the catalogue and each meaningfully changes the result set; set all three for the full DLP-classifiable view. `showAllDlpEnforceableApis` also *thins each item*: with it set, `runtimeUrls`, `primaryRuntimeUrl` and `doNotUseApiHubNetRuntimeUrl` are dropped from every entry, so the larger list is the smaller payload per connector.

The response is not paged — the whole catalogue arrives in one ~3 MB `value` array.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: An unknown or empty value is rejected with `InvalidApiVersion`, whose message echoes the full list of versions provider `Microsoft.PowerApps` accepts; the enum here is that list. Older versions stay routable and appear to be routing labels rather than contracts — the app list answers identically on `2016-11-01`, `2023-06-01` and `2025-04-01`.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description: Scopes the request to one environment. The only recognised form is `environment eq '<environmentId>'`. `~Default` may be used in place of the id to mean the tenant's default environment. Not optional here: omitting it is a `MissingEnvironmentFilter` error rather than an unfiltered list.

parameters.name: showApisWithToS
parameters.description: Includes connectors that carry publisher terms of use (the ones with a `termsOfUseUrl`), which are otherwise omitted. Measured effect on a production tenant: 319 additional connectors, exactly the set carrying `termsOfUseUrl`.

parameters.name: hideDlpExemptApis
parameters.description: Drops the connectors that DLP policy cannot classify because the platform depends on them. On a production tenant this removed exactly five: `shared_logicflows`, `shared_powerflows`, `shared_powervirtualagents`, `shared_conversionservice` and `shared_contentconversionservice`. Set it when building a DLP policy UI so exempt connectors are not offered for classification.

parameters.name: showAllDlpEnforceableApis
parameters.description: Includes every connector DLP *can* enforce against, not just those already surfaced to makers in the environment — 110 additional connectors on a production tenant. It also strips the runtime-URL properties from each returned item, because a DLP-enforceable connector need not have a runtime endpoint provisioned in the environment.

200.description: The connector catalogue for the environment.

400.description: `MissingEnvironmentFilter` — the `$filter` query parameter is not optional on this path.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, malformed or expired; the service answers `InvalidAuthenticationToken`. An entirely absent `Authorization` header produces the same 401 rather than a challenge.

404.description: `ServiceToServiceEnvironmentNotFound` — the environment named in `$filter` does not exist in the caller's tenant. Note this is a different error code from the apps path's `EnvironmentNotFound`, and it is not wrapped in `details`.

get.description:
Reads one connector. Beyond the list representation this returns `swagger` — the connector's complete OpenAPI 2.0 document, including every operation, parameter and definition — plus the environment-specific `runtimeUrls`, `primaryRuntimeUrl` and `doNotUseApiHubNetRuntimeUrl`. For a large first-party connector the document dominates the payload: the SharePoint connector answers ~300 KB against ~4 KB for its list entry.

The `$filter` requirement is the same as on the list, because the runtime URLs are per environment.

parameters.description: The connector's `name`, which is the last segment of its `id`. First-party and marketplace connectors are prefixed `shared_`; custom connectors created in an environment are not.

Older versions stay routable and appear to be routing labels rather than contracts — the app list answers identically on `2016-11-01`, `2023-06-01` and `2025-04-01`.

get.description:
Lists the environments visible to the caller, in the PowerApps API's own projection. It overlaps but does not agree with BAPI's `/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments`: this shape carries `azureRegionHint`, `runtimeEndpoints` and `cluster`, and omits the BAPI admin fields. The list projection also differs slightly from the single read — the list reports `azureRegionHint` where the read reports `azureRegion`, and the read adds `clientUris`, `databaseType` and the expanded `governanceConfiguration.settings`.

The whole list is returned in one `value` array with no pagination.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: An unknown or empty value is rejected with `InvalidApiVersion`, whose message echoes the full list of versions provider `Microsoft.PowerApps` accepts; the enum here is that list. Older versions stay routable and appear to be routing labels rather than contracts — the app list answers identically on `2016-11-01`, `2023-06-01` and `2025-04-01`.

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: `permissions` adds a `permissions` object to each environment naming every capability the caller holds in it — roughly doubling the payload. It is a capability map, not a role assignment list: keys such as `CreatePowerApp`, `DeleteAnyFlow`, `SetDLPPolicy` and `AdminReadEnvironment` are present when granted and absent when not.

get.description:
Lists the canvas apps of one environment through the tenant admin scope, which returns every app in the environment regardless of who owns or has shared it.

The response is a single flat `value` array: there is no continuation token, `nextLink` or `@odata.*` envelope, and `$top` is accepted without changing it. The `$filter` and `$expand` grammar is the narrow app-specific one described on those parameters, not general OData — an unsupported `$filter` key is silently ignored rather than rejected, so a typo yields the unfiltered list.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Environment id. This is the `name` of an environment resource, not its Dataverse organization id.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: An unknown or empty value is rejected with `InvalidApiVersion`, whose message echoes the full list of versions provider `Microsoft.PowerApps` accepts; the enum here is that list. Older versions stay routable and appear to be routing labels rather than contracts — the app list answers identically on `2016-11-01`, `2023-06-01` and `2025-04-01`.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description: Only two forms are recognised: a `tagname`/`tagvalue` pair, or `Visibility` on its own. Any other key is silently ignored rather than rejected, so a typo yields the unfiltered list. Cannot be combined with `$expand` — the service supports one query type per request and rejects the pair with `InvalidAppFilterCombination`.

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: Expands each app's sharing permissions. The single accepted form is `permissions($filter=maxAssignedTo('<objectId>'))`, which limits the expansion to grants held by that Entra object id. Cannot be combined with `$filter`.

parameters.name: $top
parameters.description: Accepted; page size cap.

200.description: The apps in the environment. An environment with no canvas apps returns `{"value": []}` rather than a 404.

400.description: `InvalidApiVersion` for an unknown or empty `api-version`, or `InvalidAppFilterCombination` when `$filter` and `$expand` are sent together.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, malformed or expired; the service answers `InvalidAuthenticationToken`. An entirely absent `Authorization` header produces the same 401 rather than a challenge.

403.description: The caller is authenticated but is not a Power Platform admin, so the admin scope is closed to it.

404.description: `BusinessAppPlatformRequestFailed`, wrapping an `EnvironmentNotFound` in `details`: no environment with that id exists in the caller's tenant. The wrapper carries a correlation id in its message.

azure_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The PowerApps API accepts tokens for the PowerApps service audience, the same audience BAPI accepts.

ErrorResponse.description: The error envelope every failing PowerApps API call returns. A 404 with an empty body means no such route exists; a 404 with this envelope means the route exists and the resource does not.

Error.description: A single error. Deeper failures nest: the outer error is a generic wrapper such as `BusinessAppPlatformRequestFailed` and the specific cause sits in `details`.

code.description: A stable, non-localised symbol. Known codes include `InvalidApiVersion`, `InvalidAppFilterCombination`, `MissingEnvironmentFilter`, `ApiResourceNotFound`, `ApplicationNotFound`, `EnvironmentNotFound`, `ServiceToServiceEnvironmentNotFound`, `BusinessAppPlatformRequestFailed`, `MultipleErrorsOccurred`, `FullNonLocalizedError`, `InvalidAuthenticationToken` and `Forbidden`.

message.description: Human-readable and localised. Several codes put machine-usable content here anyway: `InvalidApiVersion` enumerates every accepted `api-version`, `InvalidAppFilterCombination` states the supported `$filter`/`$expand` grammar, and wrapper errors embed a correlation id.

details.description: Nested causes. A `FullNonLocalizedError` entry carries the unlocalised error object re-serialised as a JSON *string* in its `message`.

Principal.description: An Entra identity referenced by a Power Platform resource. Which fields are populated varies with the caller's directory visibility: `email`/`userPrincipalName` are frequently absent even when `id` and `displayName` are present.

type.description: The resource type of the principal reference.

userType.description: Directory membership relative to the resource's tenant.

AppList.description: A page of canvas apps. Flat and complete — no continuation token or `@odata.*` metadata is returned.

App.description: A canvas app. Model-driven apps are Dataverse solution components and do not appear here.

name.description: The app id; unique per tenant.

x-notes.note: `tags` is a sibling of `properties`, not nested inside it.

AppProperties.description: The properties of a canvas app: its display name, the principals who own, created, last modified and last published it, the corresponding timestamps, and a reference to the environment that holds it.

owner.description: The current owner. Distinct from `createdBy`: ownership can be reassigned by an admin.

lastPublishedBy.description: Who last published the app. An app can be modified without being published, so this trails `lastModifiedBy`.

lastPublishTime.description: When the app was last published. Absent or empty on an app that has only ever been saved as a draft — a published version is what players run, so this, not `lastModifiedTime`, is what end users see.

appVersion.description: The published version, identified by its timestamp rather than a number.

lastDraftVersion.description: The newest saved version, published or not.

lifeCycleId.description: `Published` on an app with a live version.
lifeCycleId.x-enum-evidence: Only `Published` was seen in a recorded sample; `AppVersion.lifeCycleId` on the versions route also uses `Draft`.

createdByClientVersion.description: Studio build that created the app.

minClientVersion.description: Oldest player build that can run it.

commitMessage.description: The maker's note on the last publish.

sharedUsersCount.description: A count only — the principals themselves come from the app's `permissions` route.

appOpenProtocolUri.description: `ms-apps:///providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/apps/<appId>`, for the desktop and mobile players.

connectionReferences.description: The connectors the app binds to, keyed by connection id. This is what makes an app's connector dependencies readable without opening the `.msapp`.

x-notes.note: The probe tenant held no canvas apps, so nothing below `App` was observed here. `displayName`, the principal fields and the timestamps come from the Terraform provider's DTOs; everything added since — tags, versioning, client versions, `appUris`, the counts, the open URIs and `connectionReferences` — comes from a recorded response sample in a third-party CLI's test fixtures.

AppEnvironmentRef.description: The environment an app belongs to, denormalised onto the app so a cross-environment list stays self-describing.

location.description: Azure geography of the environment, lower-case and without spaces.

ConnectorList.description: The connector catalogue for one environment. Returned whole — around 1700 entries and 3 MB on a normal tenant — with no pagination.

Connector.description: A connector, called an 'API' throughout this surface. Covers first-party Microsoft connectors, certified marketplace connectors, independent-publisher connectors and an environment's own custom connectors.

name.description: The catalogue name. First-party and marketplace connectors are prefixed `shared_`; custom connectors are not. This is the value DLP policies use to name a connector.

ConnectorProperties.description: Connector metadata. Nothing here is marked required: the field counts in the descriptions come from a full catalogue read of a production tenant, and the fields present on every one of ~1700 connectors are `displayName`, `iconUri`, `iconBrandColor`, `apiEnvironment`, `isCustomApi`, `blobUrisAreProxied`, `connectionParameters`, `metadata`, `capabilities`, `createdTime`, `changedTime`, `tier`, `publisher`, `rateLimit` and `apiVersion`.

description.description: Marketing prose; absent on a handful of connectors.

iconUri.description: Publicly reachable PNG on `static.powerapps.com`, versioned by connector release.

iconBrandColor.description: Hex colour the maker portal tiles the icon against. Casing is inconsistent across the catalogue (`#da3b01`, `#0078D4`) and it is sometimes the empty string.

tier.description: Licensing tier, and the single most consequential field here: `Premium` connectors require a per-user or per-app Power Apps / Power Automate licence, `Standard` ones are covered by seeded Microsoft 365 licences. On a current catalogue the great majority are Premium (1487 of 1710 observed).

publisher.description: Free text, not an identifier — the same publisher appears as both `Microsoft` and `Microsoft Corporation`, and independent publishers appear under personal names. Use `metadata.source` to tell first-party from community connectors, not this.

releaseTag.description: Release channel. `Preview` connectors may change or be withdrawn and are the majority of the catalogue. One catalogue entry carries the lower-case `preview`, so match case-insensitively.

capabilities.description: What the connector can do, and therefore where it can be used. `actions` and `triggers` are the Power Automate verbs; `tabular` means it exposes CDP tabular data sources usable as a Power Apps data source; `blob` the CDP blob equivalent; `cloud` and `gateway` are the reachability modes (a `gateway` connector can reach on-premises data through an installed data gateway, `vnetgateway` through a virtual-network gateway); `federatedKnowledgeSource` marks it usable as a Copilot knowledge source; `graphconnector` as a Microsoft Graph connector. Singular `action`/`trigger` spellings occur on a few entries and mean the same as the plural forms.

isCustomApi.description: True for a custom connector created inside an environment, false for anything from the shared catalogue. Usable as a `$filter` key on this path: `isCustomApi eq 'true'`.

apiEnvironment.description: Where the connector's runtime lives. Every catalogue connector observed is `Shared`.

termsOfUseUrl.description: Present on the 319 connectors whose publisher imposes terms of use. These are excluded from the list unless `showApisWithToS=true` is sent.

changedTime.description: Last catalogue update — bumped by connector releases, not by anything in the caller's tenant.

rateLimit.description: Zero on every catalogue connector observed; real throttling is expressed in the connector's own swagger, not here.

apiVersion.description: The literal string `None` on every catalogue connector observed, not a version number and not null.

blobUrisAreProxied.description: Whether blob URIs the connector returns are rewritten to go back through the API Hub proxy rather than pointing at the backing store directly. False on every catalogue connector observed.

scopes.description: The consent text shown to a user creating a connection. Present on 397 of ~1700 connectors.

connectionParameters.description: The inputs required to create a connection, keyed by parameter name. Compound keys use a colon (`token:TenantId`) to denote a value derived from another parameter.

connectionParameterSets.description: Present on the 115 connectors that offer a choice of authentication method. When present it supersedes `connectionParameters` for connection creation.

interfaces.description: The Connected Data Platform contracts the connector implements, keyed by interface name — `CDPTabular1` for tabular data sources, `CDPBlob0`/`CDPBlob1` for blob ones. Only the ~60 connectors usable as Power Apps data sources carry a non-empty value.

swagger.description: The connector's full OpenAPI 2.0 document: `paths`, `definitions`, `x-ms-capabilities` and `x-ms-connector-metadata`. Returned only by the single-connector read, never by the list.

runtimeUrls.description: Per-environment API Hub endpoints the connection actually calls, of the form `https://<environmentId>.<n>.common.<geo>.azure-apihub.net/apim/<connector>`. Returned by the single read, and by the list only when `showAllDlpEnforceableApis` is *not* set.

primaryRuntimeUrl.description: The first entry of `runtimeUrls`; same visibility rule.

doNotUseApiHubNetRuntimeUrl.description: A deprecated alias of `primaryRuntimeUrl`, named for the `azure-apihub.net` host callers are told not to depend on. Same visibility rule.

ConnectorScopes.description: The plain-language consent summary a user sees when creating a connection.

will.description: What the connector will do with the user's data.

wont.description: What it explicitly will not do; usually empty.

ConnectorMetadata.description: Publishing and lifecycle metadata about the connector itself, as opposed to what it connects to.

source.description: How the connector reached the catalogue, and the reliable way to distinguish community content from certified content: `marketplace` is a Microsoft-certified connector, `independentpublisher` is a community-submitted one, and `manual` is hand-registered.

useNewApimVersion.description: Whether the connector runs on the newer API Management runtime. A *string*, not a boolean, and only ever the value `true` when present.

stackOwner.description: The team or company that owns the backing service, which can differ from `publisher` when a partner publishes a connector for someone else's product.

allowSharing.description: Whether a connection made with this connector may be shared with other users. Absent on most connectors; when absent the platform default applies.

hideKey.description: A gate string. A connector carrying one is hidden from the maker experience unless the tenant or request supplies the matching key, which is how private previews, deprecated connectors (`Deprecated`) and internal-only connectors are kept out of the catalogue. Casing varies (`hideKey`, `HideKey`, `hidekey`).

publicSourceSite.description: For independent-publisher connectors, where the source lives.

connectionLimits.description: Caps on how many connections may exist, keyed by scope; the only key observed is `*`, meaning all scopes.

isSponsoredConnector.description: Marks a connector whose publisher sponsors its inclusion. Present on two catalogue entries.

isNative.description: Marks a connector built into the platform rather than published to it. Present on one catalogue entry.

fileMediaTypes.description: MIME types the connector handles as file content.

OperationIcons.description: Per-operation icon overrides, keyed by operation id. Note the capitalised key.

regionSettings.description: Region-specific overrides for the connector's availability or endpoints.

ConnectorVersion.description: Connector build identifiers, of the form `releases/v<major>.<minor>.<build>\<full build number>`.

ConnectionParameter.description: One input needed to create a connection.

type.description: How the value is collected and stored. `securestring` is masked and write-only; `oauthSetting` means the platform runs an OAuth flow instead of prompting; `gatewaySetting` binds the connection to an on-premises data gateway; `connection` chains to another connection.

uiDefinition.description: Label, description, tooltip and `constraints` for the prompt. `constraints.required` is the *string* `"true"`, and `constraints.capability` restricts the parameter to particular `capabilities` values such as `cloud` or `gateway`.

allowedValues.description: Closed value list for the prompt.

defaultValue.description: Pre-filled value for the prompt; type follows `type`.

ConnectionParameterSets.description: A choice between alternative authentication methods. The user picks one named set and supplies only that set's parameters.

values.description: Each entry has a `name` (e.g. `oauth`, `BasicAuthentication`), a `uiDefinition` and its own `parameters` map of `ConnectionParameter`.

ConnectorInterface.description: One Connected Data Platform interface implementation.

revisions.description: Keyed by revision number as a string.

ConnectionList.description: Connection instances. A connection is a user's stored, authenticated binding to one connector in one environment.

name.description: The connection id: a 32-character lower-case hex string, not a hyphenated GUID.

ConnectionProperties.description: The state of a connection. `apiId`, `displayName`, `iconUri`, `statuses`, `keywordsRemaining`, `isSsoConnection`, `createdBy`, `createdTime`, `lastModifiedTime`, `environment` and `allowSharing` were present on every connection observed; the rest vary by connector and authentication mode.

apiId.description: Resource path of the connector this connection is for.

displayName.description: Usually the account the connection authenticates as, not a name the user chose.

statuses.description: Current health. A connection needing re-authentication reports something other than `Connected` here, which is what makes this the field to audit.

accountName.description: The upstream account identifier, when the connector reports one.

expirationTime.description: When the stored credential lapses and the connection must be re-authorised. Present only for connections whose credential expires — 12 of 21 observed.

keywordsRemaining.description: Remaining search-keyword budget for connectors that meter it.

isSsoConnection.description: True when the connection reuses the signed-in user's identity rather than a separately consented credential.

allowSharing.description: Whether this connection may be shared with other users.

connectionParameters.description: The non-secret parameter values the connection was created with; secrets are never returned. Present on about half the connections observed, most often just `sku`.

connectionParametersSet.description: Which `connectionParameterSets` entry was chosen, for connectors offering a choice of authentication method. Note the singular `Set` here against the plural on the connector.

testLinks.description: Ready-made requests that verify the connection is still usable.

ConnectionStatus.description: One health entry for a connection. A working connection carries exactly one entry.

TestLink.description: A pre-built request that exercises a connection.

requestUri.description: An API Hub URL ending in `/testconnection`; it embeds the environment id and the connection id.

EnvironmentRef.description: A short reference to an environment.

EnvironmentList.description: The environments visible to the caller, returned whole.

Environment.description: An environment as the PowerApps API projects it.

permissions.description: Only present when `$expand=permissions` was requested. A capability map: each key is a capability the caller holds in this environment and its value is `{"displayName": ...}`. Keys observed include `ReadEnvironment`, `UpdateEnvironment`, `DeleteEnvironment`, `CreatePowerApp`, `CreateFlow`, `CreateBot`, `CreateCustomApi`, `CreateGateway`, `CreateFunction`, `CreateSharePointCustomFormCanvasApp`, `GenerateResourceStorage`, `ExportEnvironmentPackage`, `ImportEnvironmentPackage`, `AdminReadEnvironment`, `SetDLPPolicy`, `ListAnyPowerApp`, `ListAnyFlow`, `DeleteAnyPowerApp`, `DeleteAnyFlow`, `AddEnvironmentRoleAssignment`, `RemoveEnvironmentRoleAssignment`, `ReadEnvironmentRoleInformation` and `ModifyDatabaseRoleAssignments`. A capability the caller lacks is absent rather than false.

EnvironmentProperties.description: Environment properties. The list and the single read differ: the list returns `azureRegionHint`, the read returns `azureRegion` and adds `clientUris`, `databaseType` and the nested `governanceConfiguration.settings`.

azureRegionHint.description: Concrete Azure region backing the environment, finer-grained than `location`. List projection only.

azureRegion.description: The same value under the name the single read uses.

environmentSku.description: Capacity and lifecycle class. `Default` is the tenant's single auto-created environment, which cannot be deleted; `Developer` is a free per-maker environment; `Trial` expires; `Sandbox` can be reset and copied; `Production` cannot be reset.

environmentType.description: The service ring, not the SKU — a `Sandbox` environment is still `Production` here.

provisioningState.description: Lifecycle state. Only `Succeeded` environments are usable.

creationType.description: `DefaultTenant` marks the environment the platform created with the tenant; `User` marks one someone provisioned.

isDefault.description: True for exactly one environment per tenant — the one `~Default` resolves to.

lifecycleAuthority.description: Which system owns the environment's lifecycle. `Environment` means Power Platform itself, as opposed to an environment whose lifecycle is driven by a linked external resource.

retentionPeriod.description: ISO 8601 duration a soft-deleted environment stays recoverable before it is purged.

databaseType.description: `CommonDataService` once Dataverse is provisioned; `None` before. Single read only.

usedBy.description: The single maker a `Developer` environment belongs to. Absent on shared environments.

parentEnvironmentGroup.description: The environment group this environment is a member of, if any; group membership is how rule-based governance policies are applied in bulk.

clientUris.description: Deep links into the portals for this environment. Single read only.

linkedEnvironmentMetadata.description: The Dataverse organization backing the environment. Absent entirely when no database has been provisioned — that absence, rather than a null, is how you detect a Dataverse-less environment.

updateCadence.description: Which servicing wave the environment rides. `Frequent` is first release, `Moderate` the standard schedule — this is how early an environment receives platform updates.

protectionStatus.description: Encryption-key custody for the environment's data.

keyManagedBy.description: `Microsoft` for service-managed keys; a customer-managed key set through an enterprise policy reports otherwise.

notificationMetadata.description: State of the environment's in-product notification banner. Observed as an explicit `null` on one environment, so read it defensively.

appDraftingCopilotEnabled.description: Whether makers may use Copilot to draft apps in this environment.

enableAnalyticsForMakers.description: Whether makers, not just admins, can see app usage analytics here.

RuntimeEndpoints.description: Per-service base URLs for the environment, keyed by service name. Every environment-scoped call to Dataverse, Power Automate or Copilot Studio should be addressed through the endpoint given here rather than a constructed hostname, because they are cluster- and geography-specific.

microsoft.PowerAppsAdvisor.description: App checker / advisor recommendations for this environment.

LinkedEnvironmentMetadata.description: The Dataverse organization linked to the environment. The single environment read returns a narrower projection than the list: `type`, `hostNameSuffix`, `webApiVersion`, `bapSolutionId`, `creationTemplates` and `modifiedTime` appear only in the list.

resourceId.description: The Dataverse organization id. Distinct from the environment id, and the value Dataverse's own APIs key on.

uniqueName.description: The organization's unique name; the first label of `domainName`.

domainName.description: The organization host label, not a full hostname. The Dataverse host is `<domainName>.<hostNameSuffix>`.

hostNameSuffix.description: Geography-specific Dataverse domain; the numeric suffix identifies the CRM scale group serving the region.

instanceApiUrl.description: Base for the Dataverse Web API. Note the different host from `instanceUrl` — `<domain>.api.<suffix>` rather than `<domain>.<suffix>`.

version.description: Dataverse platform build; changes with every service update wave.

webApiVersion.description: OData version segment to address the Web API with, e.g. `https://<instanceApiUrl>/api/data/v9.0/`.

baseLanguage.description: LCID of the organization's base language, fixed at provisioning and not changeable afterwards. 1033 is en-US.

bapSolutionId.description: Identifies the platform solution package installed into the Dataverse organization when the environment was linked.

creationTemplates.description: The first-party templates applied at provisioning. `D365_CDS` is a plain Dataverse database with no Dynamics 365 app installed.

securityGroupId.description: Entra security group gating access to the Dataverse organization. The all-zeros GUID, or the field's absence, means no group restriction — every licensed user in the tenant can be added.

EnvironmentStates.description: The environment's two independent state machines: whether it is provisioned, and whether it is running.

runtime.description: Whether apps and flows in the environment execute. An administratively disabled environment still exists and is still listed.

runtimeReasonCode.description: Why the runtime is in that state; `NotSpecified` when simply enabled.

EnvironmentCluster.description: The service cluster hosting the environment. Determines which physical endpoints serve it and which servicing wave it belongs to; two environments in the same `location` can sit on different clusters.

category.description: Servicing ring. `FirstRelease` clusters receive platform updates before `Prod` ones.

uriSuffix.description: The suffix that composes environment-specific service hostnames.

environment.description: Deployment ring of the cluster's own service instance, as opposed to `category`, which is its update wave.

GovernanceConfiguration.description: Managed Environments configuration: the governance controls an admin can turn on for an environment.

protectionLevel.description: Whether Managed Environments is on. `Basic` is an unmanaged environment; `Standard` is a Managed Environment, which unlocks sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker enforcement and usage insights — and requires premium licensing for every user of the environment.

settings.description: Present on the single read only.

ExtendedGovernanceSettings.description:
Managed Environments controls. Every value is a *string*, including the booleans (`"true"`/`"false"`, lower case) and the numbers.

Only the settings an admin has actually configured are returned, so an absent key means the platform default applies rather than false.

limitSharingMode.description: How far a canvas app in this environment may be shared. `noLimit` places no restriction; `excludeSharingToSecurityGroups` forbids sharing to security groups, forcing makers to name individual users.

maxLimitUserSharing.description: Ceiling on how many individual users one canvas app may be shared with, as a decimal string. `-1` means no ceiling. Only meaningful while `limitSharingMode` restricts sharing.

isGroupSharingDisabled.description: `true` blocks sharing apps with security groups outright.

disableAiGeneratedDescriptions.description: `true` stops the platform generating app and flow descriptions with AI.

excludeEnvironmentFromAnalysis.description: `true` keeps this environment out of tenant-level analytics and advisor recommendations — set it on environments whose usage would distort tenant reporting.

suppressValidationEmails.description: `true` stops the platform emailing makers about validation failures.

solutionCheckerMode.description: Solution checker enforcement on solution import: `none` does not run it, `warn` runs it and lets the import proceed, `block` fails the import on a violation.

GatewayList.description: On-premises data gateways, returned in a `value` envelope.

AppTags.description: Maker-authored and studio-authored tags, all values stringified — booleans arrive as `"true"`/`"false"` and numbers as decimal strings. Observed keys: `primaryDeviceWidth`, `primaryDeviceHeight`, `sienaVersion`, `deviceCapabilities`, `supportsPortrait`, `supportsLandscape`, `primaryFormFactor`, `publisherVersion`, `minimumRequiredApiVersion`, `hasComponent`, `hasUnlockedComponent`. The key set is open, and `$filter` on the app list matches against a `tagname`/`tagvalue` pair here.

ClientVersion.description: A Power Apps Studio build number, exploded into the .NET `Version` fields rather than sent as a string.

AppUris.description: Storage URIs for the app document and its images. The URIs carry a time-limited SAS query string, so treat them as credentials and do not log them.

readonlyValue.description: Secondary-region replica of the same document.

ConnectionReference.description: One connector the app binds to, keyed in `connectionReferences` by connection id.

id.description: Connector resource path. Lower-cased here (`/providers/microsoft.powerapps/apis/...`) where the connector catalogue returns it capitalised.

PermissionList.description: Role assignments on one resource, in a `value` envelope. The same shape serves apps, connectors and connections.

roleName.description: `CanView`, `CanViewWithShare`, `CanEdit` and `Owner` are the values the PowerShell module writes; a read may return others.

scope.description: The resource path the assignment applies to. The PowerShell module recovers the app and environment names by splitting this string, so it is the only place a per-app read states its own environment.

notifyShareTargetOption.description: Echoes the share-notification choice; `NotSpecified` when the grant did not set one.

x-notes.note: `roleName`, `scope` and the `principal` sub-fields are read by the PowerShell module; `notifyShareTargetOption`, `inviteGuestToTenant`, `createdOn` and `createdBy` come from a third-party client's recorded app-permission sample and were not seen on the connector or connection variants.

ModifyPermissionsRequest.description: Grant and revoke in one envelope: `put` adds or changes assignments, `delete` removes them by id, and a client that only grants sends an empty `delete` (and vice versa). Every `modifyPermissions` route on this host — app, connector and connection — takes this body.

delete.description: Assignments to remove, by permission id alone.

NotifyShareTargetOption.description: Capitalised here and lower-cased (`notifyShareTargetOption`) on the read — the request and response spell the same field differently.

x-notes.note: Tenant-wide sharing is expressed through `principal`, and inconsistently: sharing a connection sets `principal.id` to the tenant id with `email` empty; sharing a connector sets `email` to a single space; sharing an app sends the four-character string `"null"` in `principal.id`, and a user share sends `"null"` in `tenantId`. A client that sends a real JSON null instead is not reproducing what the module sends.

AppVersionList.description: The saved versions of one app, newest first, in a `value` envelope.

lifeCycleId.description: Which version is live. Exactly one version is `Published`; the rest are `Draft`.
lifeCycleId.x-enum-evidence: Both values are compared as literals in the PowerShell module; the set may be larger.

AppVersion.description: PascalCase where its siblings are camelCase — the wire field really is spelled this way.

NotificationList.description: In-product notifications for one directory object. The envelope key is spelled `Value` with a capital V by the reader; PowerShell is case-insensitive, so which case the service actually sends is not established here.

AppSettingsRequest.description: A single setting, sent as one dynamic key/value pair whose **key is caller-supplied** — there is no fixed field name to document. The PowerShell module builds the body as `@{ $AppSettingName = $AppSettingValue }`, so the schema is open by construction rather than because the fields are unknown.

EmptyRequest.description: An explicitly empty JSON object. The route takes no input, but the client sends `{}` and a bodyless POST was not tried.
